newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Electrabel says Tractebel merger would be complex.
newsitem.headline: Electrabel says Tractebel merger would be complex.

text.p: Belgian utility company Electrabel NV said on Wednesday that a merger with its parent, Belgian utility holding company, Tractebel SA would be a complex operation.

"Our chief executive Jean-Pierre Hansen has said previously that if you talk about rationalisation, there is a logic in (a merger). But it would be an extraordinarily complex operation in light of the relations between Electrabel and the municipal distribution companies," an Electrabel spokesman told Reuters.
Earlier a spokeswoman for Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said the government favoured a merger.

She said Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique (SGB) and French Compagnie de Suez had indicated that they had no objection to such a merger. Tractebel is owned by SGB, which is owned by Suez.

However in Paris, Suez said it aimed to keep at least 50 percent of Tractebel and denied a report in Belgian newspaper Financieel Economische Tijd that it had given written approval to a merger between Tractebel and Electrabel .
Electrabel, which has the largest capitalisation on the Brussels bourse, has a virtual monopoly on electricity production in Belgium.
